To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ODMF can be used as a generic framework for matching competency information, that the matching strategy based on the similarity of the competency descriptions is the best performing matching strategy, and that the matching strategy combining the competency descriptions and the competency hierarchy is the second best performing matching strategy.
the ODMF can be used as a generic framework to implement different data matching strategies.

(1) the ODMF provides a flexible, generic, ontology-based framework to calculate the similarity among data elements, (2) a combination of different strategies, based on the ontology, provides the most accurate results, (3) the ODMFLib is a Java library to calculate the similarity based on the ontology and (4) the ODMFMatcher is a Java tool that uses the ODMF to calculate the similarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the design of a generic ontology-based framework for data matching, (ii) the evaluation of several data matching strategies, (iii) the implementation of the matching strategies, (iv) the evaluation of the matching results, and (v) the application of the matching strategies to a real-world competency-based HRM scenario.
the design and evaluation of an ontology-based data matching approach.

the design and implementation of an ontology-based data matching strategy, which allows the calculation of similarity between competency elements, based on competency information, and which is applicable in the domain of competency-based HRM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ontology-based data matching is a viable and promising alternative to traditional matching approaches.
the ODMF can be used to support the calculation of similarity between data elements.
there is no single best matching strategy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to show the feasibility of the approach and that we can recommend to further develop and evaluate the approach in other domains.
the ODMF can be used as a framework for matching competency-based data elements and is a valuable tool to improve data quality in HRM systems.
the use of the ontology-based data matching strategy is a valuable addition to the existing data matching methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ODMF can be used to calculate the degree of similarity between competency-based information, e.g. a competency profile, a job profile or a qualification, and that the ODMFs matching strategies outperform traditional string-matching algorithms.
the ODMF allows to match different types of data elements and can be used in various domains.
a generic ontology-based approach is a feasible solution for data matching in the context of Competency-based HR Management.
